text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Elections for head of Labour party in June.
- Palestinian President Arafat calls for international arbitration on delay on Hebron deal.

- Day after Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu request, prison authority eases conditions for activist of outlawed anti-Arab Kach movement who being held in jail without trial under emergency regulations.
- Treasury heads recommend full health tax be imposed on pensioners who work.
- Army on Sunday to allow Jews to resume activities at Joseph's tomb site in Nablus Palestinian self-rule enclave for first time since September clashes.

- Labour party head Peres: The good of the country demands a unity government. Body of article quotes Peres saying, "I'm not trying to worm my way into unity governnment...Good of state demands unity."
- Calls increase for national unity government.
- Sixth graders learning about atom bomb and mustard gas.
- Combined index rises one percent in two months after freeze in April, August.
- Labour party leadership elections set for June.
- Analysis: Chances now lower for national unity government.
